quest.title: In Pursuit of a Phantom
quest.description: When you agreed to help Hu Tao and followed her to the Adventurers' Guild, you hadn't counted on becoming part of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's "business development" efforts. No topic is too sensitive for Hu Tao — certainly not matters of life and death — and even though some of her points make sense, you find them somewhat difficult to stomach. Then, when you voice your doubts about her approach, she tells you that she has long since moved on from business development to her next objective: finding someone called "Big G."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x27825, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Talk to Meng at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and find out what happened

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Meng, I'm back! I'm afraid we're still no closer to finding Big G.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I see. Well, I'm just sorry for the trouble. We've already searched in all the likely places...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who is this Big G anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I guess I should start at the beginning. My home was in the vicinity of Wuwang Hill. In my youth, I had a good many friends there.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Big G was one of them. We were the best of friends, inseparable really. But one day there was an accident, and that was the end of him.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I've never forgotten... Too many memories, I suppose. I often return to Wuwang Hill.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: But recently, after one such visit, I started to feel strange. Now, every night, Big G appears in my dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I can't help but wonder, did I disturb him somehow?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Perhaps. I don't have proof, but I can't stop worrying. I get more anxious every day.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: How would I ever come to terms with my childhood friend becoming an evil spirit?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's why he joined Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. In place of a salary, I'm helping him deal with this matter.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And in fact, what Meng has said is entirely plausible. Spirits, on occasion, do find a way into our world.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But as for evil spirits, I think you're scaring yourself. Even I have only encountered malevolent forces a handful of times.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: But are you sure there's no danger? I couldn't bear for him to go around harming people.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: You see what I mean? Look at the state of him. If we can't find Big G, it'll eat away at Meng forever.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Those people we found today were also Meng's childhood friends. I thought there was a good chance Big G might have hidden among them. But here we are, empty-handed.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Wuwang Hill, childhood friends... Seems like we're out of leads...
Sorry, excuse me, is this Wangsheng Funeral Parlor?

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: My name's Luocheng. I've had this awful feeling recently, like something's staring at me.

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: Some of my friends and I went to Wuwang Hill the other day on a dare. After I returned home, I fell ill... I've been having recurring nightmares, but the doctors can't find anything wrong with me.

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: I think that... it's a curse, right? I've been cursed by a demon!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Say no more. There's no doubt, it's a demonic curse alright — and a serious one at that.

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: You believe so too!? Then it's just like they say in the tales of old... The vengeful spirits of the gods who fell in the Archon War return to cast their evil curses upon mortals...

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: And if the curse isn't lifted, it will burn through the body, laying waste to flesh and bone! Oh, what a wretched end!

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: The symptoms I'm having are just like those described in the tales!

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Wuwang Hill? Hmm... No, I don't think it was a curse, it was probably just Big G—

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hold your horses, both of you. There's no need to creep each other out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't that exactly what you like to do, though?

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor specializes in demonic stuff like this, right? Help me, I beg you! I'm too young to die!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Alright alright, don't panic. Leave it to me, you've come to the right person.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: However, in order to lift the curse, we need a suitable location... and we need to make some preparations.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Come with me, my trusty assistants. I'm going to need your help.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: I—I guess I'll come too...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Help him make the preparations first. The incense exorcism, the one I taught you.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: When you're ready, come and find me. Once we've finished with this, we'll get back to the Big G matter.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Okay, I guess.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Right, let's go.

choices.text: That kind of thing doesn't happen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... what mysterious rituals are you gonna perform here?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: No ritual at all. We just need to kill some time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Wait, you didn't take all that vengeful god's curse stuff seriously, did you? They were eradicated ages ago!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So why are we here?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You saw those two. One thinks he's been cursed, the other one believes his friend's turned into an evil spirit. It's hard to reason with them.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: *sigh* Now you see why I believe that ordinary folks should be kept in the dark...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I've seen too many people lose their senses on account of things like this. If you want to calm them down, you need to convince them with something tangible.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And the best way to do that is to make a great show of destroying the bogeyman they believe in before their very eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Sounds like that might work if you were trying to cheer up a three-year-old...

choices.text: Isn't it better to tell people the truth?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're onto something. After all, we're only afraid of what we don't know.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Because you can't guarantee that telling an ignorant person the truth will improve the situation instead of exacerbating it.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: What I can do is pretend to pull back anyone who believes their time is nigh. But, since the curse is imaginary, our fix will also be make-believe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense, but... why would anyone believe that it's a curse?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Do you know the history of the Yaksha?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: They once fought against the ancient gods. They fought brilliantly in a battle that engulfed the whole world in darkness. Although the gods were defeated in the end, their resentment persevered.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That resentment turned into a pestilence spreading amongst the ordinary folk. Hysteric people mistook it for "the curse of the gods."

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: The plague took the lives of many, which only furthered its spread, as the dead were a breeding ground for the disease.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Then, someone discovered how to prevent it from spreading: purify the air and burn the bodies of the deceased. The pioneers of these practices were, you guessed it, the founders of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon didn't see that coming. Really?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Yes. Anyway, it took many years, but eventually the plague was completely eradicated.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: We've dealt with similar phenomena multiple times throughout the ages. Each time, we successfully restore the balance between life and death.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: To sum it up, we are "gatekeepers," guarding the border for the sake of both the living and the dead, hehe.

choices.text: That's what you meant by "guarding the border"?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So when I say this "curse" is just a figment of the imagination, I say it with more certainty than most. But I also can't really go telling people that the ancient plagues were real, or it would incite panic.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Anyway, let's wait a bit more and get ready for the show. This Ley Line Monolith will make for a really great prop.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ah, you're finally here! We just finished our preparations.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Now, look here. This device is used to drive away evil spirits. It'll absorb the curse inside you and cause it to take a physical form.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But don't worry, the Traveler here is a seasoned warrior and will assure our safety.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Oh, right. I forgot to tell you, haha! It'll be fine.

response.speaker: Luocheng
response.text: Will that really solve my problem?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Trust the director. She might look like a weirdo, but she's serious about everything she does.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Ugh, how can you call me a weirdo? I mean, wouldn't you say it's more... charmingly naive? Or... disarmingly different?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Alright, let's get down to business! My glamorous assistant, please activate the device!

choices.text: You failed to mention we'd need to fight.
Never knew Wangsheng had such a long history.
I know just some bits and pieces.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why would you ask that!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon just wants to know why we can't tell everyone the truth!

talks.objective: Protect the Ley Line Monolith and fend off the enemies
Listen as Hu Tao tells Luocheng the truth about the exorcism

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: How are you feeling? Did the curse leave your body?

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: Yes, I feel more invigorated than ever before! I'm cured!

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: I can't express how grateful I am for your and the Traveler's help! If it hadn't been for you, the curse would've taken my life.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Ah, great! In which case, I guess now I can tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: *fanfare* You've been pranked!

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: Eh? Wh—What?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: This exorcism device? People like you wouldn't recognize it, but it's just an old Ley Line Monolith, deceptively effective at attracting monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: And those were real monsters, not a manifestation of your curse.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So riddle me this: If I didn't do anything to lift the curse, then what's the cause of your sudden recovery?

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: The curse... wasn't real?

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: ...Then why was I sick?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You caught a cold, ate something bad, or just scared yourself sick, it's anyone's guess... but I'm leaning towards the last option. It wouldn't be the first time in my career.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: How unexpected...

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: I also didn't expect that, but still... I'd like to thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. I found a way to deal with your fears this time, but I can't do it over and over again, so I'd appreciate it if you try not to give in to superstitions in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Human life is short. Enjoy it while it lasts.

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: Wow, I... What a weird thing to say.

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: I—I shall head back. I'm sorry for troubling you.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I feel relieved to see that it wasn't Big G's doing. However, unless he crosses the border, there will be no end to his antics.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Since we are done with the matter at hand, can we resume our search for Big G?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I believe that won't be needed.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: He found us first.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Big G!?

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: U—Um... I didn't mean to bother you... Any of you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is Big G? He's just a child!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Well, he is a spirit. It's quite normal that he looks just like he did when he left this world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm, that's not what Paimon imagined when Paimon first heard the name "Big G."

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Let's bring him back to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. We have much to do.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi
dialogues.text: You're still here? That's it, I'm calling the Millelith.

dialogues.speaker: Luocheng
dialogues.text: Please help me, I don't want to die...

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Don't worry, the director is highly skilled, she'll help you find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Observe Device
dialogues.text: (No matter how you look at it, this is just an ordinary Ley Line Monolith.)
